text:
Priya: FYI vendor NordicCloud AS sent an invoice to Redwood Ltd and is asking us to "gross-up" for a supposed 15% Norwegian withholding. They didn't charge VAT on the invoice. Should we pay net+gross-up? :confused:

Ben: Don't pay grossed-up amount unless documented. We need the vendor to prove a legal withholding requirement. Ask for tax residency cert and the legal basis.

Priya: Invoice snippet from Coupa: ```
Invoice#: 2026-03-12-NC
Supplier: NordicCloud AS
Org/Reg: 921234567
Amount: EUR 8,500
Description: Remote platform engineering services
Vendor note: "Please gross-up 15% to cover Norwegian WHT so vendor receives net amount."
```

AP: I put the invoice on HOLD in the AP queue. Please confirm next steps for documentation we should request.

TaxTeam: Quick guidance: Norway may levy WHT on some cross-border payments, but it's not automatic for generic consulting. Key things to request: (1) Certificate of tax residency (issued by Norwegian tax authorities or commercial registrar), (2) a copy of the Norwegian tax assessment/case showing WHT applies to this service, OR (3) a contract clause specifying vendor bears WHT or requires gross-up. Without that we don't gross-up.

TaxTeam: Also ask vendor if they can issue an invoice showing VAT treatment. Since invoice is to Redwood Ltd (UK), the reverse charge / import VAT rules might apply instead of Norwegian WHT. Vendor should clarify why they think Norwegian WHT applies when the paying entity is in the UK.

Priya: Draft reply I'll send: "We cannot gross-up by default. Please provide (a) official evidence from Norw. tax authority or a tax residency certificate and calculation supporting your 15% WHT claim, or (b) a contract clause that requires gross-up. Alternatively, reissue invoice specifying VAT/reverse-charge treatment if applicable. Payment will remain on hold until validated."

Ben: Sounds good. If vendor provides a residency certificate but no legal basis for WHT, we still won't gross-up. Residency cert typically helps them claim reduced WHT when the payer is the withholder, but doesn't force us to gross-up.

AP: HOLD flag set by AP for invoice 2026-03-12-NC. Reason: awaiting vendor tax docs.

invoice-bot: Payment status: ON HOLD for invoice 2026-03-12-NC by AP 3: tax documentation requested.

Priya: Tagging Legal if they push back. Ben / TaxTeam, please advise if we need to request a withholding tax certificate or treaty article (e.g., Norway-UK tax treaty) reference.

TaxTeam: If vendor cites treaty relief, ask them to cite the treaty article and provide the formal certificate of residence and any local certificate proving they are entitled to relief. Legal can review contract language if they insist on commercial gross-up.

Priya: Thanks everyone. I'll send the note and post vendor reply in this thread.
